summary.text: A healthy 26-year-old woman who was a non-smoker, took no medication and had a body mass index of 24.7 kg/m^(2) was recruited and screened as a super-donor for fecal microbiota transplantation, with an interview, Rome IV questionnaire, physical examination, laboratory tests and serologies.

Stool microbiological analysis for Shigella, Salmonella, Campylobacter, Yersinia and C. difficile, a Helicobacter pylori stool antigen test, and a search for rotavirus and parasite eggs were all negative. Oral swab scraping and the first morning stool were collected, and the sample was used in 11 fecal microbiota recipients.

Sequencing of the 16S rRNA V3 and V4 regions identified 56 oral and 48 fecal species. The mouth was dominated by Veillonella, Haemophilus and Streptococcus with Fusobacterium nucleatum at 2.33%, while feces were dominated by Firmicutes and Bacteroidota, with Faecalibacterium prausnitzii at 9.87% and Bacteroides vulgatus at 11.8%.

article_limitations: Single healthy stool donor; the 11 FMT recipients are mentioned only as a cohort and are not annotated as individuals.
Sequencing methods (DNA extraction, primers, PCR, bioinformatics) are laboratory methods and are not recorded as patient facts.
The abstract and results disagree on the most abundant fecal species (source conflict, review_only).
The Rome IV questionnaire, examination, laboratory tests and serologies have no stated results.
The screening exclusion sentence is garbled; the 6-month window is not assigned to one item.
Discussion text on microbial functions, disease associations and cited literature describes published work, not the donor.
Pixels are reviewed in the separate visual submission; caption-layer visual status stays not_inspected. Krona-style charts have unreadable labels.
Supplementary taxon tables (Table_1.xlsx) are reviewed in the supplement manifest, not transcribed as facts.

Roster reported_individual_count left null: the only literal count statement is "A single super-donor was recruited", which the single-case pattern of the roster check does not accept (super-donor is not in its noun list), and no other sentence states the number; roster_complete stays true with one annotated individual.
Supplement SM1 (Table_1.xlsx) has no supplement content-review format for XLSX files; it is reviewed only through the supplement manifest.
